requirement:
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.

`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
For each definition with corrections, stderr MUST identify additions applied,
markers already present, outstanding manual instructions, and each unapplied
action with its reason, even at default verbosity. If a subject remains negative
with no changed inputs, the report MUST say why it paused. In `--stdout` mode,
report proposed additions as proposals. Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence,
validation, or exit-status rules.

rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.reporting` has no implementation roots, and I found no structural obligation that needs one. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface to delegate through. Each clause describes what a user observes:

- Default stderr output: true judgment lines are suppressed, and each false judgment's subject and outcome is shown.
- Progress counters, completion summaries, FIXME notices and errors stay visible.
- Single-subject metadata is retained.
- `-v` and `--verbose` add false rationales to stderr and nothing else.
- In `--stdout` mode, stdout holds only the evidence JSON and diagnostics go to stderr.
- Per-definition correction reporting.
- A reason is given when a subject pauses.
- Proposals are reported as proposals.
- Verbosity does not change persistence, validation or exit status.

The nearest candidate is "Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result, without additional inference." I treated it as behavioral. A different implementation could build the report from some other structure, or from a stored copy of the result, and a user would see the same output. Only an extra model call would violate the clause. That would show up as extra usage records and a changed result, so it can be checked by running the command and does not depend on how the code is built.

The cited requirements, `requirements.authoring.invocation` and `requirements.authoring.batch`, supply context only. I found no implementation edges on `requirements.authoring.reporting`, and none are needed.

behavioral: I judged the marked tests adequate for each behavioral obligation of `requirements.authoring.reporting`. I did not read implementation source. Findings by obligation:

- **Default suppression of `true` lines and display of `false` subject and outcome on stderr.**
  - Redirected batch: `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose]` asserts `requirements.alpha: false (usage:` is present and `: true (usage:` is absent.
  - Terminal batch: `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors]` runs in a pty and asserts the same.
  - Single-subject: `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]`, `fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` and `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` check that stderr has `SUBJECT: false` only for false judgments and never `SUBJECT: true` or `— true`.
- **Progress counters, completion summaries, FIXME notices and authoring errors stay visible.**
  - The pty test asserts `6/6 finished`, the final counts `true 3`, `false 1`, `FIXME 1` and `errors 1`, and `requirements.beta: FIXME`.
  - It also asserts `fixture model rejected` and the stdout summary line.
  - The batch tests assert the FIXME and error lines for redirected output.
  - The single-subject stdout test asserts `— FIXME` for a FIXME judgment.
- **Single-subject metadata.**
  - `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts the stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL` and has `Evidence:` and `Usage:` lines.
  - The stdout-mode test asserts the same metadata on stderr, plus `Evidence: stdout` and an existing usage file.
- **`-v` and `--verbose` show the false rationale; it is omitted by default.**
  - The single-author test covers `-v` and `--verbose` with a false judgment, and `-v` with a true judgment. It asserts the rationale appears only for false.
  - `batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose` runs both verbose and non-verbose and asserts the false rationale is present only when verbose.
  - It asserts the true rationale (`requirements.gamma`) never appears and no source text (`pub fn alpha()`) appears.
  - `fn[verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress]` covers the pty case.
- **No true rationales and no input snapshots.** Both are asserted in the tests above and in the single-author test.
- **No additional inference.** The tests assert exact request counts (`server.finish().len()` is 1 or 2, and `server.subjects().len()` is 6).
- **`--stdout` mode.** The stdout test parses stdout as JSON and requires the evidence file to be unchanged. It asserts that the metadata, the false line and the verbose rationale go to stderr, and it covers verbose with false and with true judgments.
- **Corrections reporting at default verbosity.**
  - `fn[corrections_replay_reference_only_mixed_and_regression_findings]` asserts `(applied)` for additions.
  - It asserts `paused for manual work: <instruction>` for outstanding manual instructions.
  - It asserts the `paused; requested markers already present, no assessment inputs changed` line, which covers the paused-with-no-changed-inputs case.
  - It asserts the "assessor must inspect this exact item" reason for unread targets.
  - It asserts `paused with unapplied correction` with a reason for a missing node.
  - It asserts `proposed correction: Add `{test}`` and no `(applied)` in stdout mode.
  - `fn[read_only_correction_pauses_the_subject_after_applying_writable_siblings]` covers read-only reasons alongside an applied sibling.
  - `fn[unreachable_reference_targets_are_reported_without_writing_or_retrying]` covers the unapplied reasons: bad path, invalid selector, no match and ambiguous.
- **Verbosity does not change persistence, validation or exit status.**
  - Batch tests run with and without `--verbose` and assert the same nonzero exit status and the same evidence.
  - The single-author test asserts exit success, the evidence content, and the `validate_repository` outcome for both verbose and non-verbose runs.

I found no obligation without a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome. A case combining an already-present marker with other applied additions is only indirectly asserted. That case is not a distinct obligation beyond the covered report lines.

{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation` {cite}`requirements.authoring.batch`
:::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} batch
`habeas author --all [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [-v|--verbose]` MUST author
the evidence of every current requirement and named example, together with the
reviews {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review` include, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`.
`--all` MUST be mutually exclusive with a subject name and `--stdout`. It MUST
also delete each orphaned citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and each orphaned site review
under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and report each deletion; the
deletion MUST NOT require model configuration or credentials.
Failure to discover declarations or to read, scan, or parse project sources MUST report an error,
not a successful empty batch.
Each subject MUST receive an independent assessment with its own prompt, inputs,
judgment, and usage record. The command MUST report aggregate completion and each
authoring error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.reporting`, and retain
successful writes when another assessment fails. It MUST return a nonzero
exit status if any assessment fails. False judgments MUST still be written as
completed assessments; they remain failures under ordinary evidence validation.
A denied mandatory input MUST abort only the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`. Interruption MUST instead stop the
whole batch: queued assessments MUST NOT start, running assessments MUST be
cancelled, and an assessment whose evidence has not been written when the
interruption is observed MUST NOT begin committing it. After preparing a
temporary evidence file, the harness MUST check interruption again before its
atomic replacement; a replacement already in progress MAY finish. Evidence already written MUST be
retained, and the command MUST report the number of assessments not started as
a batch failure.
The bundled Habeas skills MUST direct the supervising agent to run this command
to create or refresh evidence. They MUST leave judgments, rationales, and input
snapshots to the authoring harness; the supervising agent addresses outstanding manual findings by
changing requirements, source citations, implementation, or tests.
